rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two already-evaluated archive signals ("Two-Dimensional Research Financing Mismatch" and "Rent-Scarce Research Rollover") that merely rank-weights one leg of the existing ensemble, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism, and the near-duplicate construction makes any incremental t-stat gain uninformative.

The archive already contains both MIN-conjunctions of unabsorbed external financing with the rollover leg (ls_talpha -3.09) and with the R&D-shock source leg (ls_talpha -3.18); averaging the two conditioners is a third permutation of the same conjunction family with no new economic content, and the deep nesting makes the driver of any result impossible to attribute.

Combining the equity-cushion and maturity-share buffers is a defensible attempt to reconcile the alpha-strong and slope-strong archive results, but because both legs are multiplied by the same VOL(xrd/sale) term the composite is largely a rescaled R&D-volatility (and low-leverage) signal, so the test should be read as a check on whether the buffers add anything beyond R&D-volatility/leverage exposure.

Because ceq/(|ceq|+lt) is bounded in (0,1] for almost all firms, the product is uniformly non-positive and monotonically increasing in weakness of the cushion only through a multiplicative shrink toward zero — so zero-dividend or low-R&D-volatility firms are pooled with the intended "fragile dividend payer" short leg, contradicting the stated "favorable and unfavorable tails" reasoning.

This is a legitimate substantive swap of the buffer leg in the archived "Reinvestment-Validated Uncertainty Support" structure, motivated by a real alpha-versus-slope diagnostic, though the MIN conjunction risks discarding exactly the well-capitalized firms that generated the base signal's alpha and the result will need attribution against the standalone cushion×VOL leg.

This is straightforward ensembling of two already-evaluated archive signals ("Dual-Validated Intangible Deleveraging" and equity-cushion×R&D-volatility) with no interaction between them beyond rank averaging, so a strong result would be arithmetically implied rather than economically informative.
